prompt: The first artifact of a good automation project is…

options.text: …an honest map of the current process with volumes, times, and error rates: revealing which (usually small) steps are judgment-shaped

explanation: You place AI into a process; understanding the process comes first. The map plus the volume/ambiguity/error-cost scoring finds the AI-shaped hole.

prompt: A fully deterministic step ('copy field A into system B') should be implemented with…

options.text: …plain code: a model adds cost and a nonzero failure rate to something software does perfectly
…a large language model for future flexibility

explanation: Deterministic work gets deterministic tools. Model calls are spent only on judgment-shaped steps: the economic version of 'workflow before agent'.

prompt: Why must the manual baseline be measured BEFORE building the automation?

options.text: Once automation rolls out, the honest 'before' is gone, and without it, ROI is an unprovable feeling

explanation: Minutes/item, error rate, cycle time (measured up front) are what turn 'it feels faster' into a business case a CFO can verify.

prompt: Webhooks are delivered 'at least once'. The engineering consequence is…

options.text: …duplicates will arrive, so processing must be idempotent: dedupe on event ID before acting and use idempotency keys on external calls
…you should ask senders to guarantee exactly-once
…a short sleep before processing prevents duplicates

explanation: At-least-once is a law of distributed delivery. You can't prevent the duplicate; you make it harmless: running twice must equal running once.

prompt: What does putting a queue between trigger and processing buy you?

options.text: Spikes become backlog instead of dropped requests; failures land in a dead-letter queue for inspection; workers scale independently

explanation: Decoupling receipt from processing is the standard absorber for bursty reality, with the dead-letter queue as the visible place failures go instead of vanishing.

prompt: A model step returns low-confidence extraction for one item. Correct handling is to…

options.text: …route that item to a human review queue with the document and draft, and record the correction: low confidence is permanent for the item, so retrying just resamples uncertainty

explanation: Transient failures retry, while permanent or ambiguous conditions route to a safe outcome. Confidence routing limits automatic processing to cases that pass defined checks, and reviewed corrections can become evaluation data. The resulting quality must be measured rather than assumed.

prompt: Automation handles 78% of items clean; 22% go to a 3-minute human review. This is…

options.text: …the design working: the review queue is what makes the 78% trustworthy, and the hours saved are the result, not a failure to reach 100%
…a reason to remove the review step and accept errors

explanation: The goal was measured value, not full autonomy. Removing the safety valve to chase 100% trades a working system for incidents.

prompt: Which costs belong in an honest automation ROI?

options.text: API tokens, hosting, the review queue's human minutes, and ongoing maintenance time: alongside the savings

explanation: All-in accounting is what keeps stakeholder trust when someone redoes your napkin math, and they will.

prompt: Why keep the manual process executable after rollout?

options.text: Upstream formats and providers WILL have bad days; a fallback turns degradation into an operations event instead of a business stoppage
To double every item's processing cost forever

explanation: An automation with no fallback is a new single point of failure. Drift and outages were promised by earlier modules; the fallback prices them in.

prompt: Pilot success criteria should be defined before the pilot runs because…

options.text: …pre-registration prevents both sunk-cost 'success' declarations and anecdote-driven cancellations
…criteria cannot be typed after a pilot starts

explanation: Deciding what 'good' means before seeing results is basic experimental honesty: the pilot-scale version of not tuning on the test set.

prompt: Which elements make a workflow survive its own crashes and upstream failures? Select all that apply.

options.text: Durable per-run state in a database
Bounded retries with backoff for transient errors, then dead-letter
Keeping all progress in worker memory for speed

explanation: State in the database (resumable), bounded retries (self-healing), idempotency (safe replays). In-memory-only state is exactly what crashes erase.

prompt: The strongest predictor that an automation gets adopted rather than resisted is…

options.text: …the operators co-designed it, keep an override, and their new reviewer role is explicit: it's visibly their tool
…hiding the error rate from the team

explanation: Adoption is a change-management outcome. Automation done WITH the team sticks; automation done TO the team gets quietly worked around.

prompt: Incoming webhooks should be verified (signature/secret) because…

options.text: …your trigger URL is reachable by anyone: unverified, an attacker can inject fabricated events that your pipeline dutifully processes

explanation: A webhook endpoint is an open door; the signature is the key check. Trigger authenticity is part of the trust boundary.

prompt: The idempotency key for a workflow step is best composed of…

options.text: …the event/record ID plus the step name, so each step of each item is dedupable independently, and a retried step 3 can't skip because step 2 already ran

explanation: Keys must be deterministic per logical operation: same work → same key → deduped; different steps → different keys. Random keys defeat the whole purpose.

prompt: 'Automation rate' (share auto-processed) rose from 78% to 91% after loosening the confidence threshold. What must be checked before celebrating?

options.text: The error rate among auto-processed items: throughput gains from a looser threshold may just be errors reclassified as successes
Nothing; higher automation is the goal

explanation: The threshold trades review load against error rate (precision/recall in business clothing). Moving it changes BOTH numbers; report them together.

prompt: A well-designed human review queue item contains…

options.text: …the source document, the model's draft with confidence, the reason it routed here, and one-click approve/correct: everything needed to decide in seconds
…only the record ID, to avoid bias
…a blank form to re-enter from scratch

explanation: Review UX determines whether the queue is a 3-minute task or a 15-minute one, and corrections captured here feed the eval set.

prompt: The manual fallback path should be rehearsed periodically because…

options.text: …an unexercised fallback rots (people forget, credentials expire, volumes outgrow it), and you discover that during the outage, which is the worst time
…a written runbook guarantees the fallback will work without rehearsal

explanation: A fallback is a capability, and capabilities decay without exercise: the same logic as incident game days (Module 16).

prompt: A growing exception/review queue with stable input volume is an early signal of…

options.text: …drift: inputs are changing shape (new formats, segments) faster than the automation handles them: investigate the queue's contents as diagnostic data

explanation: The queue is a drift detector: what lands there is precisely what the system no longer handles. Its composition is a prioritized to-do list.

prompt: Batch (nightly) versus realtime (webhook) triggering should be chosen by…

options.text: …the business latency requirement: if decisions can wait hours, batch is simpler, cheaper, and easier to operate; realtime earns its complexity only when freshness pays

explanation: Latency requirements are business requirements. Overpaying for unneeded freshness is the infrastructure version of using a frontier model for classification.

prompt: In n8n-style visual workflows, the error-workflow (a flow triggered by failures) exists to…

options.text: …give failures a designed path (notify owners, record context, route to humans) instead of dying silently inside a node

explanation: Same principle as code: failure paths are designed, not hoped away. Visual tools just make the design literal: a red wire to somewhere intentional.
